wholeCurrentGoal.title: Proteine und Genwirkketten für Merkmale erklären
wholeCurrentGoal.titleEn: Explain Proteins and Gene Chains for Trait Expression
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann Aufgaben von Proteinen sowie das Zusammenwirken von Genen in einer Genwirkkette bei der Ausbildung von Merkmalen erläutern und Auswirkungen einer Unterbrechung der Genwirkkette erklären.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can explain protein functions and gene interactions in a gene chain during trait expression and explain effects of interrupting such a gene chain.

decisions.science: Two-step S→I→P chain correctly links geneA/E1 and geneB/E2. The interrupted model leaves E1 and intermediate formation intact but removes the E2 step; feeding I cannot replace E2. Dashed absent-product symbols do not depict actual blue pigment production.
decisions.phoneReadability: At360/680 the critical E1/E2, geneB loss, no blue pigment and I cannot replace E2 labels are readable. Large intervention statement and color/arrow/x redundancy make the counterfactual legible.
decisions.perspectiveAndHumanRepresentation: No stigmatizing human depiction, clinical diagnosis or real learner-performance claim. Abstract cells/chromosomes and optional silhouettes serve the biological relation; visible labels communicate limits where needed.
decisions.formatAndStyle: 1672×941 landscape, clear instructional comic/schematic drawing, strong navy text, sparse panels/arrows, consistent palette; aspect supports the native goal resource.
decisions.limitations: Specific constructed loss-of-function pigment model; not every mutation necessarily removes its enzyme. Gene-expression intermediate steps omitted schematically.
decisions.existingFindingResolution: Targeted preceding scientific/phone V defect is materially addressed in these actual pixels; original FIRST remains history.

wholeCurrentGoal.title: Genaktivität für Zelldifferenzierung und Anpassung erklären
wholeCurrentGoal.titleEn: Explain Gene Activity for Cell Differentiation and Adaptation
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann Mechanismen der Regulation der Genaktivität beschreiben und damit erklären, wie Zellen trotz gleicher genetischer Ausstattung unterschiedliche Eigenschaften aufweisen, sich an Umweltbedingungen anpassen und lebendige Systeme entwickeln und spezialisieren können.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can describe mechanisms of gene activity regulation and use them to explain how cells with the same genetic information develop different properties, adapt to environmental conditions, and enable development and specialization in living systems.

decisions.science: Same-DNA comparison is explicitly limited to one gene. Open versus dense chromatin, TF binding, transcription arrow and different mRNA/protein amounts form a coherent gene-regulation explanation. Signal is a schematic input rather than a claim of automatic genome change.
decisions.phoneReadability: TF=Transkriptionsfaktor is large and fully readable at360; identical DNA, cellA/B, chromatin open/dense and high/low protein labels remain distinguishable. The essential regulatory message no longer depends on tiny TF abbreviation.
decisions.perspectiveAndHumanRepresentation: No stigmatizing human depiction, clinical diagnosis or real learner-performance claim. Abstract cells/chromosomes and optional silhouettes serve the biological relation; visible labels communicate limits where needed.
decisions.formatAndStyle: 1672×941 landscape, clear instructional comic/schematic drawing, strong navy text, sparse panels/arrows, consistent palette; aspect supports the native goal resource.
decisions.limitations: Transcriptional regulation of one gene; does not assert all neuronal versus muscle gene expression, complete signaling mechanisms, or absolute zero transcription.
decisions.existingFindingResolution: Targeted preceding scientific/phone V defect is materially addressed in these actual pixels; original FIRST remains history.

wholeCurrentGoal.title: DNA-Replikation, PCR und Reparaturenzyme vergleichen
wholeCurrentGoal.titleEn: Compare DNA Replication, PCR, and Repair Enzymes
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann den natürlichen Prozess der DNA-Replikation mit der PCR vergleichen, Probleme und Lösungen technischer Umsetzung natürlicher Prozesse erklären und die Bedeutung von Reparaturenzymen bei der natürlichen DNA-Replikation beschreiben.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can compare natural DNA replication with PCR, explain problems and solutions in technically implementing natural processes, and describe the importance of repair enzymes in natural DNA replication.

decisions.science: Cellular fork versus cyclic PCR is clearly separated. Helicase/polymerase are labelled; visible95/55/72°C cycle and paired opposing primer/extension arrows are schematic typical PCR conditions. Right removal/fill/closure sequence illustrates repair without a clinical or universal perfection claim.
decisions.phoneReadability: All three headings, Helicase/Polymerase and95/55/72°C are readable at360/680. Enzyme arrows and repeated cycle are large.
decisions.perspectiveAndHumanRepresentation: No stigmatizing human depiction, clinical diagnosis or real learner-performance claim. Abstract cells/chromosomes and optional silhouettes serve the biological relation; visible labels communicate limits where needed.
decisions.formatAndStyle: 1672×941 landscape, clear instructional comic/schematic drawing, strong navy text, sparse panels/arrows, consistent palette; aspect supports the native goal resource.
decisions.limitations: Schematic natural synthesis/repair and typical selected PCR temperatures; not a complete strand/Okazaki/proofreading/base-excision mechanism or a real laboratory action receipt.
decisions.existingFindingResolution: Targeted preceding scientific/phone V defect is materially addressed in these actual pixels; original FIRST remains history.

wholeCurrentGoal.title: Meiose geschlechtsspezifisch erklären
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann den Ablauf der Meiose bei unterschiedlichen Geschlechtern beschreiben und ihre Bedeutung für die geschlechtliche Fortpflanzung erklären.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can describe the process of meiosis in different sexes and explain its importance for sexual reproduction.

decisions.science: One homologous pair separates in meiosisI; sister chromatids separate in meiosisII. Four equal sperm-side products contrast with one large egg-side product and three smaller polar-body products. Every endpoint has one represented chromosome, matching n for the displayed pair.
decisions.phoneReadability: At360/680 I homolog separation, II chromatid separation,2n,n,sperm/egg/polar-body labels are readable. Brackets clearly classify endpoints.
decisions.perspectiveAndHumanRepresentation: No stigmatizing human depiction, clinical diagnosis or real learner-performance claim. Abstract cells/chromosomes and optional silhouettes serve the biological relation; visible labels communicate limits where needed.
decisions.formatAndStyle: 1672×941 landscape, clear instructional comic/schematic drawing, strong navy text, sparse panels/arrows, consistent palette; aspect supports the native goal resource.
decisions.limitations: Completed, highly simplified one-pair scheme; rounded sperm-side cells are genetic products, not a complete spermiogenesis shape sequence. It omits oocyte pauses/fertilization timing/crossover, so is support rather than a complete account.
decisions.existingFindingResolution: Targeted preceding scientific/phone V defect is materially addressed in these actual pixels; original FIRST remains history.

wholeCurrentGoal.title: Genetische Neukombination und Biodiversität verknüpfen
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann den Zusammenhang zwischen genetischen Neukombinationsprozessen und der Evolution bisheriger sowie zukünftiger Biodiversität erklären.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can explain the relationship between genetic recombination processes and the evolution of past and future biodiversity.

decisions.science: Four distinct chromatids retain same-locus markers. Exchange between the inner two yields one red/one blue unchanged chromatid and two reciprocally exchanged distal segments. Parentals/recombinants are grouped separately. Butterfly panel is explicitly one population; generations, inheritance and selection bridge that population to possible diversity. No one-chromatid-to-one-species arrow remains.
decisions.phoneReadability: At360/680 parentals versus newly combined, existing alleles and the population/generations/inheritance/selection/possible-diversity bridge are readable. Segment colors and marker positions distinguish unchanged and reciprocal chromatids.
decisions.perspectiveAndHumanRepresentation: No stigmatizing human depiction, clinical diagnosis or real learner-performance claim. Abstract cells/chromosomes and optional silhouettes serve the biological relation; visible labels communicate limits where needed.
decisions.formatAndStyle: 1672×941 landscape, clear instructional comic/schematic drawing, strong navy text, sparse panels/arrows, consistent palette; aspect supports the native goal resource.
decisions.limitations: Abstract reciprocal exchange, not an anatomical chiasma geometry. Recombination rearranges existing alleles and does not guarantee diversity increase/speciation. Population panel shows schematic within-population variation.
decisions.existingFindingResolution: Targeted preceding scientific/phone V defect is materially addressed in these actual pixels; original FIRST remains history.

wholeCurrentGoal.title: Genommutationen aus Karyogrammen ableiten
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann aus Karyogrammen verschiedene Typen von Genommutationen ableiten, deren Auswirkungen auf verschiedenen Organisationsebenen beschreiben und zwischen Genotypänderung, Phänotypänderung und Krankheit unterscheiden.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can derive different types of genome mutations from karyograms, describe their effects on different organizational levels, and distinguish genotype changes, phenotype changes, and disease.

decisions.science: One-type2→3 copies (trisomy) is separated from all illustrated types2→3 copies (triploidy). Gendosis→cell→organ→organism supports organizational levels. Dotted arrows end in a disease question, retaining the need for further evidence rather than equating complement with disease.
decisions.phoneReadability: At360/680 one-type versus all-types,2n/3n,Trisomie/Triploidie and the disease question are readable; color and explicit chromosome counts reinforce labels.
decisions.perspectiveAndHumanRepresentation: No stigmatizing human depiction, clinical diagnosis or real learner-performance claim. Abstract cells/chromosomes and optional silhouettes serve the biological relation; visible labels communicate limits where needed.
decisions.formatAndStyle: 1672×941 landscape, clear instructional comic/schematic drawing, strong navy text, sparse panels/arrows, consistent palette; aspect supports the native goal resource.
decisions.limitations: Three-type schematic set, not a complete patient karyogram or individual health prediction. Normal denotes the supplied two-copy reference, not a judgment of human worth.
decisions.existingFindingResolution: Targeted preceding scientific/phone V defect is materially addressed in these actual pixels; original FIRST remains history.
